RagShortTexts: The double election of 1257 left rival claims by Richard of Cornwall and Alfonso of Castile.

Variants.Content: The double election of 1257 left rival claims by Richard of Cornwall and Alfonso of Castile. Rhenish archbishops, secular princes and the Bohemian king mattered, while practice and support remained contested. Money, recognition and presence shaped kingship rather than one uncontested electoral constitution.
